rows.definition: The Related.BenchmarkWitnesses []string field on debtlane lane records (internal/debtlane/debtlane.go, wire key benchmark_witnesses) holding the benchmark-authority mention keys collected while scanning a lane (internal/debtlane/scan.go) and checked against BENCHMARK-AUTHORITY.md by the debt-clean workflow (internal/debtlane/detectors.go).
rows.distinction: A lane-scan COLLECTION of benchmark-authority mention keys, NOT a proof bundle or an obligation counter: unlike DisambiguationWitnesses (worker-land scorecard proof artifacts) it stores authority-reference strings attached to a debt lane, and unlike RequiredWitnesses (witnesses still owed) it is the raw mention list, not a remaining-due count.

rows.definition: The stopgate Disposition constant in internal/stopgate/types.go (wire value claim_unwitnessed_continue) returned when a session's done-claim lacks a confirming witness under enforce mode: the stop gate blocks the exit (exit code 2, Blocked=true) while letting the session continue to produce the missing witness (internal/stopgate/boundary.go).
rows.distinction: A stopgate DISPOSITION on the blocked-but-continuing branch, NOT a loop-gate marker or a sweep verdict: unlike LOOP_DONE_UNWITNESSED (loop-gate unwitnessed-done marker) it is a typed Disposition value that steers exit codes, and unlike ClaimWitnessed (dispatch-tick sweep verdict) it fires precisely when the claim is NOT witnessed.

rows.definition: The stopgate Disposition constant in internal/stopgate/types.go (wire value claim_unwitnessed_give_up) returned when an unwitnessed done-claim exhausts its retry budget: the gate stops blocking, allows the exit (exit code 0), and records the StageGiveUp outcome (internal/stopgate/boundary.go).
rows.distinction: The TERMINAL branch of the same unwitnessed-claim path, NOT a separate gate: it differs from DispClaimUnwitnessedContinue only in budget exhaustion - the gate stops blocking and allows the exit - and from the generic GiveUp dispositions (BlindGiveUp, SameIssueGiveUp) in that its trigger is specifically a missing done-claim witness.

rows.definition: The stopgate Disposition constant in internal/stopgate/types.go (wire value claim_witnessed) returned when a session's done-claim carries a verifying witness: the stop gate allows the exit and stamps the witness into the decision note (internal/stopgate/witness.go).
rows.distinction: The WITNESSED branch of the stopgate done-claim check, NOT a sweep verdict or a commit grader: unlike ClaimWitnessed (dispatch-tick sweep verdict over ledger rows) it is a per-session Disposition deciding exit allowance, and unlike CommitWitnessed (dispatch-tick audit-row grader) it grades the done-claim itself, not a commit.

rows.definition: The sentinel error defined in internal/observer/verdict.go that the observer pool returns when a mutating step reports success without a confirmed diff witness (internal/observer/pool.go); screen.go screens it together with the unwitnessed-claim verdict to hold the step's result (internal/observer/screen.go).
rows.distinction: A sentinel ERROR IDENTITY, NOT a verdict value or a prose reason: unlike WitnessOK (the diff-witnessed constant flagging a witnessed diff) it is the failure signal raised when the diff witness is absent, and unlike ReasonUnwitnessed (a deny reason string) it is matched with errors.Is, not compared as text.

rows.definition: The ExecutionWitness receipt field (internal/roofline/empirical.go, mirrored in internal/amdgpu/roofline_probe.go and cmd/fak/validate_acceptance.go) that must be non-empty whenever a roofline receipt claims physical device execution (Simulated=false); Verify() refuses such receipts without it.
rows.distinction: A RECEIPT FIELD attesting physical execution, NOT a witness mechanism or a whole proof document: unlike the vDSO world-state witness (external world-state token per tool call) it attests hardware execution inside a roofline receipt, and unlike FeatureProofReceipt (gateway feature-rewrite proof artifact) it is one string field gated by Simulated=false, not a receipt document.
